claims.claim: Le Guin says of her own practice that she is very strong on accuracy and exactitude.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin interviewed by John Plotz, "The Story's Where I Go", Public Books, 15 June 2015
claims.quote: I’m very strong on accuracy and exactitude.
claims.page: answer on describing an invented world

claims.claim: Le Guin says you cannot describe everything because that would be very boring.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin interviewed by John Plotz, Public Books, 15 June 2015
claims.page: answer on describing an invented world

claims.claim: Le Guin says that to write Tehanu all she had to do was describe Earthsea from the point of view of the powerless and disempowered.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, "Chronicles of Earthsea" reader Q&A, The Guardian, 9 February 2004
claims.quote: describe it from the point of view of the powerless
claims.page: answer on the gap between The Farthest Shore and Tehanu

claims.claim: Le Guin says what she has learned as a writer, as she has gone on, is that you do as little as possible.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin interviewed by Paul Morton, "Getting Away with Murder: The Millions Interviews Ursula K. Le Guin", The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: you do as little as possible
claims.page: answer near the end of the interview

claims.claim: Le Guin says she loves the sound of language and plays with word sounds in her head.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: I love language, I love the sound of language.

claims.claim: Le Guin says Woolf's Orlando gave her the authentic thrill of being taken absolutely elsewhere.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, contribution on Virginia Woolf, The Guardian, 14 May 2011
claims.quote: the authentic thrill of being taken absolutely elsewhere
